# UniGL Spoofer A Zygisk module that spoofs **GPU info (OpenGL ES / Vulkan)** and **device identity** per app, so games and other apps can unlock higher graphics settings. All code is written from scratch. **Compatibility:** works with any Zygisk implementation. Android 8.0+, arm64-v8a / x86_64.

## What gets spoofed | Area | Method | |---|---| | `glGetString` (vendor, renderer, version, extra extensions) | GOT hook + `eglGetProcAddress` + `dlsym` | | Vulkan `deviceName`, `vendorID`, `deviceID`, `driverVersion` | hook `vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(2/2KHR)` + `vkGetInstanceProcAddr` | | `android.os.Build` (MODEL, BRAND, MANUFACTURER, DEVICE, PRODUCT, BOARD, HARDWARE, SOC_*) | JNI static fields | | `ro.product.*`, `ro.hardware`, `ro.board.platform`, `ro.soc.*` | hook `__system_property_get` | ## Usage 1. Make sure Zygisk is enabled, flash the zip, and reboot. 2. Open the module's **WebUI** (KernelSU / KernelSU-Next / APatch, or WebUI-X for Magisk). 3. Add the app's package name, pick a profile, **force stop** the app, and launch it again. 4. Make sure the app is **not** on a denylist or unmount list, otherwise Zygisk will not inject the module. The configuration lives in `/data/adb/unigl/` (`targets.conf` and `profiles/*.conf`) and can be edited by hand. ## Profiles Bundled device profiles are based on the top of the AnTuTu Android ranking (October 2026, global data). Every device comes in two flavors: - **Minimal**: only the GPU strings (OpenGL ES renderer and vendor, Vulkan device name), the manufacturer, and the model. Start here. - **Full**: everything in Minimal, plus the Vulkan vendor ID, brand, board, hardware, and SoC model/manufacturer. | # | Device | Model | GPU | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | HONOR Magic9 Pro Max | WKL-AN20 | Adreno 850 | | 2 | RedMagic 11 Pro | NX809J | Adreno 840 | | 3 | POCO F9 Ultra | 26077PC53G | Adreno 840 | | 4 | iQOO 15 | I2501 | Adreno 840 | | 5 | OnePlus 15 | CPH2747 | Adreno 840 | | 6 | Xiaomi 17 Ultra | 2512BPNDAG | Adreno 840 | | 7 | POCO F8 Ultra | 25102PCBEG | Adreno 840 | | 8 | OPPO Find X9 Ultra | CPH2841 | Adreno 840 | | 9 | Samsung S26 Ultra | SM-S948B | Adreno 840 | Model numbers come from public listings (some from pre-release Geekbench entries), so double-check them if you can. Apps may not recognize brand-new GPUs, so the Adreno 840 profiles are the safest first choice. Use **Profile specs** in the WebUI to see exactly what a profile changes. Device profiles cannot be edited or deleted. For anything else, use **Custom profiles** in the WebUI to create, edit, and delete your own. Every key is optional, and an empty value leaves the real value untouched. Custom profiles are stored in `/data/adb/unigl/profiles/.conf` and are never touched by module updates. ## Limitations - Only the app's own libraries are patched, not system libraries. - 64-bit only. - Packed relocations (`DT_ANDROID_RELA`) are not supported yet, so libraries that use them are not hooked. - CPU core count, RAM, and refresh rate are not changed. - Checks that happen on a server cannot be bypassed. - Spoofing device identity in online games may violate their terms of service. Use at your own risk. ## Restore to normal / uninstall - **One app only:** open the WebUI, tap **Remove** next to the app, then force stop it. It is back to normal on its next launch, and no reboot is needed. - **Everything off:** turn the module off in your root manager and reboot. Nothing is spoofed anymore. - **Uninstall:** remove the module in your root manager and reboot. To delete your settings as well, run `su -c "rm -rf /data/adb/unigl"`. - **An app keeps crashing and you cannot open the WebUI:** run `su -c "rm /data/adb/unigl/targets.conf"` (or create the file `/data/adb/modules/unigl_spoofer/disable`) and reboot. The module only affects the apps you listed, so it cannot cause a boot loop. ## License MIT. `src/zygisk.hpp` follows the public Zygisk API v4 (0BSD, John Wu). ## Author Amon, on Telegram: [@xhamon](https://t.me/xhamon)
readmeHTML:
UniGL Spoofer

A Zygisk module that spoofs GPU info (OpenGL ES / Vulkan) and device identity per app, so games and other apps

can unlock higher graphics settings. All code is written from scratch.

Compatibility: works with any Zygisk implementation. Android 8.0+, arm64-v8a / x86_64.

What gets spoofed

| Area | Method |

|---|---|

| glGetString (vendor, renderer, version, extra extensions) | GOT hook + eglGetProcAddress + dlsym |

| Vulkan deviceName, vendorID, deviceID, driverVersion | hook vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties(2/2KHR) + vkGetInstanceProcAddr |

| android.os.Build (MODEL, BRAND, MANUFACTURER, DEVICE, PRODUCT, BOARD, HARDWARE, SOC_*) | JNI static fields |

| ro.product.*, ro.hardware, ro.board.platform, ro.soc.* | hook __system_property_get |

Usage

  • Make sure Zygisk is enabled, flash the zip, and reboot.
  • Open the module's **WebUI** (KernelSU / KernelSU-Next / APatch, or WebUI-X for Magisk).
  • Add the app's package name, pick a profile, **force stop** the app, and launch it again.
  • Make sure the app is **not** on a denylist or unmount list, otherwise Zygisk will not inject the module.

    • The configuration lives in /data/adb/unigl/ (targets.conf and profiles/*.conf) and can be edited by hand.

    Profiles

    Bundled device profiles are based on the top of the AnTuTu Android ranking (October 2026, global data).

    Every device comes in two flavors:

  • **Minimal**: only the GPU strings (OpenGL ES renderer and vendor, Vulkan device name), the manufacturer, and the model. Start here.
  • **Full**: everything in Minimal, plus the Vulkan vendor ID, brand, board, hardware, and SoC model/manufacturer.

    • | # | Device | Model | GPU |

    |---|---|---|---|

    | 1 | HONOR Magic9 Pro Max | WKL-AN20 | Adreno 850 |

    | 2 | RedMagic 11 Pro | NX809J | Adreno 840 |

    | 3 | POCO F9 Ultra | 26077PC53G | Adreno 840 |

    | 4 | iQOO 15 | I2501 | Adreno 840 |

    | 5 | OnePlus 15 | CPH2747 | Adreno 840 |

    | 6 | Xiaomi 17 Ultra | 2512BPNDAG | Adreno 840 |

    | 7 | POCO F8 Ultra | 25102PCBEG | Adreno 840 |

    | 8 | OPPO Find X9 Ultra | CPH2841 | Adreno 840 |

    | 9 | Samsung S26 Ultra | SM-S948B | Adreno 840 |

    Model numbers come from public listings (some from pre-release Geekbench entries), so double-check them if you can.

    Apps may not recognize brand-new GPUs, so the Adreno 840 profiles are the safest first choice.

    Use Profile specs in the WebUI to see exactly what a profile changes. Device profiles cannot be edited or deleted.

    For anything else, use Custom profiles in the WebUI to create, edit, and delete your own. Every key is optional,

    and an empty value leaves the real value untouched. Custom profiles are stored in /data/adb/unigl/profiles/.conf

    and are never touched by module updates.

    Limitations

  • Only the app's own libraries are patched, not system libraries.
  • 64-bit only.
  • Packed relocations (`DT_ANDROID_RELA`) are not supported yet, so libraries that use them are not hooked.
  • CPU core count, RAM, and refresh rate are not changed.
  • Checks that happen on a server cannot be bypassed.
  • Spoofing device identity in online games may violate their terms of service. Use at your own risk.

    • Restore to normal / uninstall

  • **One app only:** open the WebUI, tap **Remove** next to the app, then force stop it. It is back to normal on its next launch, and no reboot is needed.
  • **Everything off:** turn the module off in your root manager and reboot. Nothing is spoofed anymore.
  • **Uninstall:** remove the module in your root manager and reboot. To delete your settings as well, run

    • su -c "rm -rf /data/adb/unigl".

  • **An app keeps crashing and you cannot open the WebUI:** run

    • su -c "rm /data/adb/unigl/targets.conf" (or create the file /data/adb/modules/unigl_spoofer/disable) and reboot.

    The module only affects the apps you listed, so it cannot cause a boot loop.

    License

    MIT. src/zygisk.hpp follows the public Zygisk API v4 (0BSD, John Wu).

    Author

    Amon, on Telegram: @xhamon
